items.title: JTI reaffirms commitment to Nigeria’s economic growth
items.description: By Soni Daniel Japan Tobacco International (JTI) Nigeria has reaffirmed its long-term commitment to the country’s economic growth and development, expressing confidence in Nigeria’s future and pledging to sustain responsible business practices. The company, which said it had operated in Nigeria for 18 years, maintained that its continued presence reflected its confidence in the country’s economic prospects and commitment to creating sustainable value for its stakeholders. The General Manager of JTI Nigeria, Abdallah Simba, stated this while reflecting on Nigeria’s development journey and the country’s 66th Independence Anniversary. Simba said Nigeria remained an important market for the company, adding that its continued operations demonstrated confidence in the country’s long-term potential. He said JTI’s business philosophy prioritised responsible corporate conduct, regulatory compliance, employee development and constructive engagement with stakeholders. “Our commitment to Nigeria goes beyond our business operations. As Nigeria celebrates the important milestone of its 66th independence, we recognise the importance of building a responsible and sustainable enterprise that contributes positively to the country’s development while creating long-term value for our employees, partners and stakeholders,” Simba said. He explained that the company’s operations were guided by corporate governance standards, ethical business practices and respect for the country’s regulatory framework. Simba also highlighted JTI Nigeria’s commitment to fostering an inclusive workplace through professional development, diversity, equal opportunities and a culture of mutual respect. According to him, responsible corporate citizenship is essential to building sustainable businesses, particularly in highly regulated industries where compliance, transparency and accountability are critical. As Nigeria navigates an evolving economic environment, Simba expressed confidence in the country’s resilience and its capacity to create opportunities for sustainable business growth. He reaffirmed the company’s commitment to maintaining its presence in Nigeria, strengthening stakeholder relationships and contributing to the country’s long-term economic aspirations. items.title: Tinubu reaffirms skills development drive as NPRGS empowers 700 in Oyo
items.description: By Johnbosco Agbakwuru President Bola Tinubu has reaffirmed his administration’s commitment to empowering Nigerians through skills acquisition and sustainable livelihoods, as 700 beneficiaries graduated from a 10-day Federal Government vocational training programme in Oyo State. Dr Abiola Arogundade, Senior Special Assistant to the President on Technical, Vocational and Entrepreneurship Education (TVEE), stated this on Friday in Ibadan at the graduation ceremony. The training was organised under the National Poverty Reduction with Growth Strategy (NPRGS) to equip beneficiaries with practical, market-relevant skills for economic independence. Arogundade said the initiative reflected Tinubu’s determination to bridge Nigeria’s skills gap and empower young Nigerians to compete effectively in the evolving economy. She said the programme was designed to promote self-reliance, improve employability and enable beneficiaries to build sustainable livelihoods. According to her, the 700 beneficiaries comprised 30 participants trained in artificial intelligence (AI) and graphics, 85 in makeup artistry, 85 in fashion design and 500 in digital economy-related skills. “This project is very dear to my heart because I come from Aremo, Ibadan. “But it is also very dear to the heart and vision of His Excellency, President Bola Ahmed Tinubu, whose determination to close Nigeria’s skills gap is a major driver of the mandate we have been given.” Arogundade said Tinubu believed young Nigerians needed opportunities, skills and tools to compete effectively and achieve economic independence. She urged stakeholders to support initiatives that equipped young people with relevant skills and opened pathways to sustainable livelihoods. Sen. Sharafadeen Alli, APC governorship candidate in Oyo State and representative of Oyo South Senatorial District, said the initiative would contribute to poverty reduction not just in Oyo but across the country. Sen. Alli said the Tinubu administration had introduced measures to cushion the effects of petrol subsidy removal, adding that the empowerment programme was part of efforts to tackle poverty and unemployment. Similarly, Sen. Yunus Akintunde (representing Oyo Central) commended Arogundade for facilitating the programme and urged beneficiaries to preserve and make productive use of the equipment provided. The Olubadan of Ibadanland, Oba Rashidi Ladoja, represented by Shola Ladoja, also commended Arogundade and the Federal Government for the initiative, while expressing optimism that the programme would contribute to poverty reduction and improve livelihoods. The ceremony attracted youths, representatives of non-governmental organisations, politicians, traditional rulers, entrepreneurs and academics. At the end of the programme, all beneficiaries were awarded certificates and provided with start-up kits to support their transition into self-employment and sustainable livelihoods. items.title: Souveraineté numérique : Les pays ouest-africains connectent leurs stratégies
items.description: Dakar a accueilli, ce jeudi 8 octobre 2026, la réunion interministérielle constitutive du Conseil interministériel du réseau ouest-africain des « Backbones » nationaux (Roa-Bn). Cette rencontre, qui a réuni dix pays membres, a pour objectif de renforcer la synergie régionale et de promouvoir le développement des infrastructures numériques. L’avenir du numérique en Afrique de l’Ouest a été au cœur des échanges, hier, jeudi 8 octobre, lors de la réunion interministérielle constitutive du Conseil interministériel du réseau ouest-africain des « Backbones » nationaux (Roa-Bn). À Dakar, les représentants des dix pays membres de cette instance régionale se sont penchés sur les enjeux économiques et sociaux liés au développement du numérique. Ils engagent leurs États respectifs à s’investir davantage dans la mise en œuvre et la valorisation des infrastructures numériques transfrontalières. Cela, pour garantir la connectivité entre les États et offrir aux communautés des opportunités économiques. Les « Backbones3 vont fluidifier la transmission de données et d’informations qui peuvent être utilisées dans la prise de décision publique. Pour le président du Roa-Bn, Cheikh Oumar Traoré, par ailleurs directeur général de la Société malienne de transmission et de diffusion, il s’agit de faire du numérique un levier de souveraineté, de compétitivité et de développement économique. À ses yeux, la région ouest-africaine dispose d’atouts considérables ; du fait qu’elle est reliée par des infrastructures stratégiques de plus en plus performantes. Construire les autoroutes du numérique Aussi, a-t-il souligné, la région bénéficie d’investissements majeurs dans les réseaux de fibre optique et l’accès international. « Elle dispose surtout d’une jeunesse dynamique, d’un marché en pleine croissance et d’une volonté affirmée de faire du numérique un moteur de développement. Toutefois, pour exploiter pleinement ce potentiel, nous devons aller plus loin. Nous devons mutualiser davantage nos capacités. Nous devons renforcer nos interconnexions régionales. Nous devons faciliter la circulation des données à l’échelle sous-régionale. Et surtout, nous devons construire un véritable marché régional des infrastructures numériques », a ajouté M. Traoré. Face aux évolutions technologiques, les pays membres du réseau ouest-africain des « Backbones » nationaux entendent renforcer leur coopération pour bâtir une intégration numérique. La matérialisation de cette vision commune nécessite l’adoption de textes fondateurs, la validation du Plan stratégique 2026-2030 et la mise en place des instances du réseau. Une fois cette étape franchie, les membres vont miser sur l’implantation d’infrastructures publiques robustes, avec des réseaux de fibres optiques de plusieurs milliers de kilomètres interconnectées, des datacenters de dernière génération et des points d’échanges. « Sur le plan technique, notre mission est claire et quantifiable : nous devons harmoniser nos cadres réglementaires pour optimiser les liaisons transfrontalières en fibre optique, mutualiser nos capacités redondantes et poser les jalons d’un corridor d’infrastructure qui garantira le transit de la donnée ouest-africaine sur le sol ouest-africain », a souligné Samba Diouf, le ministre sénégalais des Télécommunications et du Numérique. « L’inclusion numérique, le développement des moyens de télécommunications et l’économie numérique demeurent nos objectifs principaux. Cela exige de notre part une synergie technique et financière sans précédent », a-t-il ajouté. Diégane DIOUF

items.title: 2027: APC campaign to begin in Kaduna on October 24
items.description: By Johnbosco Agbakwuru ABUJA — The All Progressives Congress (APC) presidential campaign for the re-election of President Bola Tinubu will be formally inaugurated on October 14, with the campaign officially kicking off in Kaduna on October 24. The Director-General of the APC Presidential Campaign Council, Senator Abdulaziz Yari, disclosed this after meeting with Tinubu at the State House, Abuja, saying the President had approved a timetable for campaign visits to states ahead of the 2027 general elections. Yari, a former governor of Zamfara State, said the campaign organisation would be inaugurated at the State House Banquet Hall on Wednesday, October 14, while the official flag-off would take place in Kaduna 10 days later. “The President asked for me to come and brief him on where we are, and to discuss the timetable for the state visits,” Yari said. “By God’s grace, his team, I, and Mr President himself, we have agreed on how it’s going to be done. We have put forward a proposal.” He said the campaign would move to Port Harcourt, Rivers State, after the Kaduna flag-off, before proceeding to Maiduguri, Borno State. Yari added that the full itinerary would be made public after the inauguration, noting that the proposed visits had been approved by the President and the campaign team. “By God’s grace, on the 24th of October, we’re going to do our flag-off campaign in Kaduna, inshallah,” he said. “Then we outlined our state visits to each and every place where we will go, and then the President has approved them.” On the prospects of opposition presidential candidates Peter Obi of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) and former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar of the African Democratic Congress (ADC), Yari dismissed their chances of defeating Tinubu, arguing that a presidential candidate needed nationwide support to win. He claimed that Tinubu had the backing of more than 20 states across the country, while challenging the opposition candidates to demonstrate comparable support beyond their respective regions. “Can the ADC candidate today in the southern part of the country beat his chest and say he has control of one state in the South? And I don’t think Peter Obi, who used to be my colleague, can beat his chest and say he has control of one state in northern Nigeria,” Yari said. He argued that strong support in one region would not be sufficient to secure victory in a presidential election without support from other parts of the country. Yari cited the 2011 presidential election, when the late former President Muhammadu Buhari secured substantial support in northern Nigeria but lost the national contest, to support his argument about the importance of a broad geographical spread. The former governor also defended Tinubu’s record in office, saying the APC would campaign on what it considered the administration’s achievements rather than promises. “President Bola Tinubu, since the time he assumed office, has turned around the situation that he met on ground; still, the economy is moving,” he said. “So I think we have done enough that we can tell our opponents about what we did. “We are not promising. We are doing it, and we are going to continue.” Yari was appointed Director-General of the APC Presidential Campaign Council in August 2026 to coordinate the party’s mobilisation for Tinubu’s re-election bid. He also said that President Tinubu has control of over 20 states of the federation while his opponents, Peter Obi of the Nigeria Democratic Congress, NDC, and Alhaji Atiku Abubakar of the African Democratic Congress, ADC, cannot boast of having control of any state outside their region. Yari, a former Governor of Zamfara State, disclosed this after meeting President Tinubu at the State House, saying the campaign leadership and the President had agreed on a timetable for state visits ahead of the 2027 general election. “The President asked for me to come and brief him on where we are, and to discuss the timetable for the state visits,” Yari said. “By God’s grace, his team, I, and Mr President himself, we have agreed on how it’s going to be done. We have put forward a proposal.” He said inauguration of the campaign organisation would hold on Wednesday, October 14, at the State House Banquet Hall, while the official flag-off would take place in Kaduna on October 24. “By God’s grace, on the 24th of October, we’re going to do our flag-off campaign in Kaduna, inshallah,” he said. “Then we outlined our state visits to each and every place where we will go, and then the President has approved them. So we are going to hit the ground running by the 24th of October, inshallah.” Yari said Kaduna would be followed by Port Harcourt (Rivers State) and Maiduguri (Borno State), adding that the full itinerary would be released after the inauguration. “The next state is going to be Port Harcourt. From there, we will be in Maiduguri,” he said. “We have the timetable, and we’re going to make it available after the inauguration. But these have all been understood and approved by the team of Mr President and I.” On whether the ADC presidential candidate, former Vice President Atiku Abubakar and the NDC presidential candidate, Mr. Peter Obi are threats to the President Tinubu’s re-election, the APC campaign director-general dismissed the chances of opposition figures, arguing that no candidate can win the presidency without a national spread. “We are talking of the president of the country, and this president, who, by God’s grace, Almighty God used him to support Atiku some time back, and at the same time to support Peter Obi,” Yari said. “If Allah uses me to support you, there is no how Allah will use you to bring me down. I mean, they cannot bring him down.” He challenged the opposition’s electoral strength, asking whether the African Democratic Congress candidate could claim control of any state in southern Nigeria, and whether Obi could claim any state in the North. “Can the ADC candidate today in the southern part of the country beat his chest and say he has control of one state in the South? And I don’t think Peter Obi, who used to be my colleague, can beat his chest and say he has control of one state in northern Nigeria,” Yari said. “This calculation shows us that even if you have control of 80 per cent of the South, if you don’t have anything in the North, you cannot make it. If you have 80 per cent control of the North, if you don’t have any state in the South, you cannot make it. And that’s what it is.” Yari cited the 2011 presidential election, in which the late former President Muhammadu Buhari won strong support across northern states but lost nationally, to illustrate his argument that regional strength alone is insufficient. “Look at Buhari, of blessed memory. He had control of over 70 per cent at that time, over 11 states in the North, and had no control of one in the South. He couldn’t make it all the way,” he said. “And today, I’m sure Asiwaju (Bola Tinubu) has control of more than 10 states in the South, in a conservative estimate, and I believe he has control of more than 10 states in the North. This is calculation; it is not rocket science.” The former Zamfara governor insisted that Tinubu had improved the country since taking office and that the APC would campaign on performance rather than promises. “President Bola Tinubu, since the time he assumed office, has turned around the situation that he met on ground; still, the economy is moving,” Yari said. “So I think we have done enough that we can tell our opponents about what we did.” “We are not promising. We are doing it, and we are going to continue.” Yari was appointed Director-General of the APC Presidential Campaign Council in August 2026 to lead the party’s mobilisation for Tinubu’s second-term bid. items.title: NFL legend Mike Ditka, Bears’ Super Bowl-Winning Coach, dies at 86
items.description: NFL legend Mike Ditka, who won league titles as both a player and coach with the Chicago Bears and Dallas Cowboys, has died at the age of 86. His family announced his death on Friday in a statement, describing him as a beloved husband, father, grandfather and friend. “While the world knew Mike as a Hall of Fame football player, legendary coach, and leader of the Chicago Bears’ Super Bowl XX championship team, we knew him as the heart of our family,” the family said. “Mike will be missed beyond measure and remembered forever.” Jarrett Payton, son of late Hall of Fame running back Walter Payton, who played under Ditka in Chicago, shared the family’s statement on social media. Ditka, a tight end, was selected fifth overall in the 1961 NFL Draft and played in the league from 1961 to 1972. He helped the Bears win the 1963 NFL championship and later caught a touchdown pass for the Dallas Cowboys in their 1972 Super Bowl victory. As a coach, Ditka led the Bears to victory in Super Bowl XX in January 1986, when Chicago defeated the New England Patriots 46-10 to end a 23-year championship drought. He also served as an assistant coach with the Cowboys during their Super Bowl-winning campaign in 1978, when they defeated the Denver Broncos. The Bears said Ditka’s contribution to the franchise, spanning decades as a player, coach and ambassador, was immeasurable. “His integral role in bringing world championships to our city and our franchise, both as a player and as our coach, established prominence and excellence at a world-class level,” the team said. Ditka recorded 121 wins and 95 losses as head coach of the Bears and New Orleans Saints. His forceful personality and hard-hitting approach earned him the nickname “Iron Mike” during his playing career. After coaching, he became a prominent television football analyst and commentator. His gruff manner and outspoken personality also made him a popular figure in Chicago sports culture, including as a subject of parody on Saturday Night Live. Born and raised in suburban Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania, Ditka played basketball, baseball and American football at the University of Pittsburgh. He was named the NFL Offensive Rookie of the Year in 1961 after becoming the first rookie tight end in league history to record more than 1,000 receiving yards in a season. Ditka was inducted into the College Football Hall of Fame in 1986 and the Pro Football Hall of Fame in 1988, becoming the first tight end to be inducted into the latter. Bears founder George Halas, who had coached Ditka during his playing career, appointed him head coach in 1982. During his 11 seasons in Chicago, Ditka guided the team to three conference finals and one Super Bowl title. His celebrated 1985 Bears team finished the regular season with a 15-1 record before defeating New England in the championship game. The squad also became famous for its “Super Bowl Shuffle” music video. Despite occasional clashes with assistant coaches and players, Ditka established himself as one of the most recognisable figures in American football. The Bears retired his jersey number, 89, in 2013. Ditka described the honour as “the consummation of a career” and “a tremendous honour.” He also appeared in films and television programmes, often playing himself, and endorsed numerous products, particularly in the Chicago area. AFP The post NFL legend Mike Ditka, Bears’ Super Bowl-Winning Coach, dies at 86 appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Linking LEAP to productive inclusion could cut extreme poverty by 2030 – UNICEF
items.description: The United Nations Children’s Fund (UNICEF) says linking Ghana’s Livelihood Empowerment Against Poverty (LEAP) programme with the Productive Inclusion Initiative (PII) could reduce extreme poverty by 2.5 percentage points by 2030. The organisation is urging the government to ensure that social protection laws translate into tangible support for vulnerable households. The call was made at the launch of the Social Protection Act, 2025, and the Social Protection and Affirmative Action Regulations in Accra on October 7, 2026. UNICEF welcomed the Act’s emphasis on coordination and complementarity, saying stronger links between social protection programmes could help address the multiple challenges facing vulnerable families. “We have evidence that when paired, the LEAP and PII programs have the potential to reduce extreme poverty by two and a half percentage points by 2030,” the organisation said. UNICEF illustrated the need for coordinated support with the example of a young mother whose household struggles with limited income and the cost of essential services. “She may be struggling with her income but also with the cost of nutritious food, access to health care, child care, skills, education, employment,” it said. The example highlights how vulnerable households can face several interconnected challenges that cash assistance alone may not fully address. The Social Protection Act provides for social assistance and social insurance, establishes institutional arrangements and creates a social protection fund. Vice President Professor Naana Jane Opoku-Agyemang has urged stakeholders to address gaps that limit access to social protection programmes to ensure assistance reaches its intended beneficiaries. The Ministry of Gender, Children and Social Protection is responsible for implementing the frameworks. Sector Minister Dr Agnes Naa Momo Lartey assured that the ministry would prioritise effective implementation and monitoring to help alleviate poverty and improve livelihoods. She said the ministry would make the laws accessible through clear language and local-language translations, with outreach across regions and districts to help citizens understand their rights and responsibilities. “We will support institutions to comply by providing clear guidance, practical tools, reporting templates and training for the officers who apply these rules each day,” she said. Dr Lartey added that the ministry would strengthen data systems to support fair beneficiary targeting, improve governance of the social protection fund and establish accessible complaint channels that citizens could trust. The frameworks are expected to improve the delivery of social protection programmes and help ensure support reaches vulnerable people who need it most.

items.title: Trade Ministry backs use of creative arts to rehabilitate prison inmates
items.description: The Ministry of Trade, Agribusiness and Industry has commended the Ghana Prisons Service for using creative arts to develop inmates’ skills, promote rehabilitation and prepare them for economic opportunities after their release. Deputy Trade Minister Sampson Ahi, speaking on behalf of the sector Minister, Elizabeth Ofosu-Adjare, said creative arts could help inmates rediscover their talents, rebuild confidence and develop skills that would support their reintegration into society. He made the remarks as the special guest of honour at the maiden Director-General and Adehyee’s Art Exhibition, where he highlighted the role of art in promoting human dignity, mutual understanding and personal transformation. Mr Ahi said correctional facilities must go beyond keeping people in custody to provide practical opportunities for personal development and economic independence. He also pointed to the potential of Ghana’s creative arts industry to generate employment, encourage entrepreneurship and contribute to national development. He called for art exhibitions involving inmates to become sustainable platforms for identifying talent, attracting public-private partnerships and connecting their works to commercial markets. The Deputy Minister further urged the public to look beyond the past mistakes of incarcerated persons and avoid stigmatising them, stressing the need to recognise their dignity and capacity to contribute productively to society. Director-General of the Ghana Prisons Service, Mrs Patience Baffoe-Bonnie, said the exhibition aligned with the Service’s broader “Think Prisons 360 Degrees” philosophy, which seeks to transform the institution from a predominantly custodial system into one focused on rehabilitation, development and sustainability. The initiative forms part of wider efforts by the Service to use skills training and creative arts to support inmate reformation and reintegration.

items.title: Guinée : l’ex cheffe de la diplomatie, M’Mahawa Bangoura tire sa révérence
items.description: La Guinée est en deuil. Hadja M’mahawa Bangoura, ancienne ministre des Affaires étrangères, est décédée ce vendredi 9 octobre 2026 à Conakry, des suites d’une maladie, a appris Guinéenews de sources familiales. Figure marquante de la vie politique guinéenne, elle avait dirigé la diplomatie guinéenne de 2000 à 2002, sous la présidence de Lansana Conté. Elle était reconnue pour son intégrité, sa dignité et sa fidélité à ses convictions. Véritable pionnière du leadership féminin en Guinée, Hadja M’Mahawa Bangoura a marqué l’histoire du pays à travers son parcours diplomatique et ses fonctions ministérielles. Son engagement et son expérience ont contribué à inspirer plusieurs générations de femmes. L’empreinte qu’elle a laissée au sein de l’administration guinéenne reste notamment visible dans son ancien département ministériel, où une salle de réunion porte son nom en hommage à son parcours. Pour l’heure, le programme des funérailles n’a pas encore été communiqué par la famille.

items.title: Negotiations with government to continue despite strike suspension – GNAT
items.description: The General Secretary of the Ghana National Association of Teachers (GNAT), Thomas Musah, says negotiations with the government over teachers’ outstanding demands will continue. This is despite the suspension of the strike by three teacher unions. “The issues have not been completed. Negotiations have not ended or concluded. Let me put it, not concluded. And so we’ll continue to negotiate until all the issues are done,” Mr Musah said on Accra-based Citi News on Friday, October 9. GNAT, the National Association of Graduate Teachers (NAGRAT) and the Pre-Tertiary Teachers’ Association of Ghana (PRETAG) suspended their industrial action following engagements with the Council of State and the Fair Wages and Salaries Commission (FWSC). The unions began the strike on September 25, 2026, over outstanding concerns relating to promotions, conditions of service and allowances. Mr Musah stressed that the suspension of the strike did not mean all the issues had been resolved, insisting that the unions would continue engaging the government until their demands were addressed. Under the commitments reached, promotion-related arrears are expected to be paid to 51,000 teachers by October 16, 2026, with payments to the remaining beneficiaries scheduled to be completed by the end of October. The digital support allowance is expected to be paid in November, while the continuous professional development allowance is scheduled for December 2026. The unions are expected to continue negotiations with the government on the outstanding issues following the suspension of the industrial action.

items.title: ‘Ghana cannot afford to waste public resources; every cedi has a job’ – Ato Forson
items.description: Finance Minister Dr Cassiel Ato Forson has challenged regional and local government authorities to step up efforts to recover lost public funds, tighten financial controls and ensure every cedi collected by the state is properly accounted for. He said waste and mismanagement of public resources directly undermine the delivery of essential services, warning that Ghana could no longer afford to lose money that should be improving the lives of citizens. Dr Ato Forson made the call in Tamale during an engagement on the 2025 Auditor-General’s Report with Regional Ministers, Metropolitan, Municipal and District Chief Executives (MMDCEs). Held under the theme “ Recovering Every Cedi ,” the meeting sought to strengthen financial accountability, improve compliance and ensure public funds are used for their approved purposes. “Ladies and gentlemen, Ghana does not have the luxury of wasting public resources. Every cedi already has a job waiting for it,” he said. He explained that public money should translate into tangible benefits for communities, including medicines for health facilities, classroom repairs, improved markets, drainage works and the maintenance of feeder roads. “So, when a cedi is wasted, left uncollected or poorly spent, somebody, somewhere, loses a service,” he added. The Finance Minister urged public officials to make the recovery and protection of state funds a routine administrative responsibility rather than a commitment made only at official engagements. “That is why ‘Recovering Every Cedi’ cannot remain just a slogan on today’s banner. It must become a way of working: collect what is due; protect what is collected; spend what is approved; account for what is spent; recover what is owed; and prevent it from happening again,” he stated. Dr Ato Forson stressed that accountability must extend beyond compliance with audit requirements to ensuring that financial irregularities are addressed and weaknesses that expose public resources to losses are corrected. He called on Regional Ministers, MMDCEs and Coordinating Directors to act on the findings of the Auditor-General, pursue the recovery of funds where necessary and strengthen internal controls to prevent a recurrence of financial lapses. He said responsible management of public resources was essential to improving local infrastructure and ensuring that government spending delivers meaningful results for communities. The meeting was attended by several Regional Ministers, including Northern Regional Minister Ali Adolf John; Savannah Regional Minister Salisu Be-Awuribe Issifu; North East Regional Minister Ibrahim Tia; Upper West Regional Minister Puozuing Charles Lwanga; Oti Regional Minister John Kwadwo Gyapong; and Upper East Regional Minister Akamugri Donatus Atanga.

items.title: Ghana expects economic boost as World Assemblies of God Congress brings 10,000 delegates to Accra
items.description: Ghana is expected to benefit economically from the arrival of more than 10,000 delegates from nearly 200 countries for the World Assemblies of God Congress in Accra from October 14 to 16, 2026. The three-day gathering will bring together pastors, ministers and church leaders from across the world, creating potential business opportunities for the hospitality, transport, tourism and food sectors, as well as local traders. The congress will also mark the first time in its 50-year history that the global Assemblies of God gathering is being held in Africa. Speaking on Joy FM’s A Walk With Jesus , Dr Kwadwo Boateng Bempah, Assistant Superintendent of Assemblies of God Ghana, said the global Assemblies of God fraternity had about 89 million members. “It has never come to Africa before. This is the first time in 50 years. And this is Africa’s time of revival,” he said. The congress will hold daytime leadership and breakout sessions at Black Star Square, running from the morning until about 5 p.m. Activities will then move to the Accra Sports Stadium for evening revival rallies. Dr Bempah said the event was open to Christians beyond the Assemblies of God denomination. “Everybody is invited. It is not only Assemblies of God. We are made up of different denominations,” he said. International speakers expected at the congress include Bishop Doug, Reverend Dominic Yeo from Singapore, Apostle Escobar and Dr Stephen Wengam, alongside other church leaders from around the world. The evening rallies will feature gospel musicians including Sinach, Joe Mettle, Dunsin Oyekan and Reverend Angela Donadio, as well as Gramophone Chorale. They will be joined by a 500-member Congress Mass Choir and other international gospel singers. Dr Bempah said the programme would focus on prayer, miracles, breakthrough and spiritual renewal. “It’s going to be a time of mega revival,” he said. The congress will also spotlight the Assemblies of God’s MM33 vision, which seeks to establish one million churches worldwide by 2033. Dr Bempah said the movement currently had about 500,000 churches and planned to establish another 500,000 to reach the target. “We have half a million churches now, and we want to plant an additional 500,000 churches to make it one million local churches,” he said. He explained that the 2033 target was linked to the 2,000th anniversary of the ascension of Jesus Christ. For Dr Bempah, evangelism remains central to the church’s mission. “The church exists to win souls. We don’t have any other purpose,” he said. He added: “We need to keep focused and win more souls because Jesus is coming very soon.” The World Assemblies of God Congress runs from October 14 to 16, with daytime sessions at Black Star Square and evening revival rallies at the Accra Sports Stadium. Dr Bempah has invited Christians from different denominations to attend what he described as an “epoch-making” gathering for Ghana and Africa.

items.title: Rentrée littéraire : Samba Oumar Fall frappe fort avec trois romans
items.description: Coup sur coup, l'écrivain Samba Oumar Fall annonce la parution prochaine de trois romans : Le silence de l'impuissance, 100 espoirs et Dieu n'est pas sénégalais. Trois livres très différents, qui ont en commun l'exil, la maladie et la question de ce que l'on porte en silence. Samba Oumar Fall fait une rentrée littéraire à trois titres. Les trois romans paraissent en 2026 aux éditions Edisal, et chacun explore à sa manière les épreuves qui séparent les êtres : la maladie, la migration, la peur de l'autre. Le silence de l’impuissance : un roman de mère, d'exil et de retour Après vingt ans passés en France, Salimata Fall rentre au Sénégal, terre de ses origines. C'est là qu'elle apprend qu'elle est atteinte d'un cancer incurable. Ses deux enfants vivent loin d'elle : Raby, avocate à Paris, et Doudou, installé à Montréal. Salimata décide de leur cacher la vérité, par pudeur, par amour et par peur de les voir souffrir. Dans ce silence s'installe un compagnon inattendu : le Cancer lui-même, personnage à part entière que seule Salimata voit. Il s'assoit face à elle et converse avec elle dans des dialogues dépouillés, presque philosophiques, sur la vie, la mort et le temps qui reste. Le roman paraît à l'occasion d'Octobre rose. Samba Oumar Fall a décidé de reverser l'intégralité de ses droits d'auteur à la Ligue sénégalaise contre le cancer (LISCA). « Faire en sorte que chaque exemplaire vendu devienne, aussi modestement soit-il, un geste de solidarité envers celles et ceux qui affrontent le cancer », explique-t-il. Il dédie le livre « à toutes les femmes qui traversent ou ont traversé cette épreuve ». 100 espoirs : la migration en fantasy Tous les 333 ans, un navire surgit des ténèbres : l'Éclair. Pour y embarquer, 2 020 combattants s'affrontent sur une plage, et seuls cent survivants sont élus pour une traversée vers une Terre promise. Un cavalier masqué leur annonce la règle : seuls trente-trois atteindront l'autre rive. À la barre, le Nocher, passeur immortel au cœur de pierre, guide le navire à travers un labyrinthe de dix-huit portes, une cité où l'on meurt pour un regard de trop, des cités enchantées et le royaume des ombres. Parmi les élus, Aljana, karatéka rongée par la vengeance, Rahma, enceinte et fuyant l'infamie, Dieuwrigne, aveugle de naissance, et AmulYaakar, dont le prénom wolof signifie « sans espoir ». Entre fantasy, mythologie et récit de survie, le livre se veut une allégorie de la migration : « la migration racontée autrement ». Dieu n'est pas sénégalais : entre cauchemar et réalité Makhou Sarr, 52 ans, est arrivé en Italie en avril 2000. Il a connu neuf ans de précarité avant d'être régularisé, a fondé une famille avec Léna, puis est rentré au Sénégal pour y lancer son entreprise. Quand un virus frappe le nord de l'Italie, il quitte précipitamment le pays et passe vingt-huit jours en quarantaine à l'hôpital. Un vieil imam mourant, Élimane Sarr, lui y confie une phrase qui ne le quittera plus : « Dieu n'est pas sénégalais. » À sa sortie, le pays a changé. Les marchés sont déserts, la faim pousse les familles à la révolte, et Léna, restée à Bergame, ne répond plus. Puis une vidéo révèle qu'elle a été enlevée en Libye. Makhou part la chercher jusqu'aux geôles de Benghazi. Le roman aborde la pandémie, le fatalisme sénégalais, l'exil, la foi et la responsabilité humaine. Le titre, précise le dossier de presse, n'attaque pas la foi : il invite à la réflexion. Le livre laisse un message, que Dieu est universel et qu'aucune nation n'a le monopole de Dieu, du malheur ni de la souffrance. O.B.N

items.title: Lekjaa a-t-il réussi à conduire le PAM à bon port ?
items.description: L'adhésion de Fouzi Lekjaa au Parti Authenticité et Modernité (PAM), en qualité de membre de son bureau politique, a profondément marqué la scène politique marocaine. Haut commis de l'État, ministre délégué au Budget et figure centrale de la gestion sportive nationale associée aux succès du football marocain et aux projets sportifs majeurs (CAN 2025, Coupe du Monde 2030), son ralliement à une formation partisane a immédiatement transcendé le cadre d'un simple recrutement organique. Entre redistribution des cartes au sein de la majorité à l'approche des échéances et interrogation sur la posture des technocrates face à l'engagement partisan, cet événement a agité la scène politique. Il a particulièrement interpellé les spécialistes du marketing politique et électoral, soulevant un vif débat sur la porosité entre action publique, communication d'image et ambitions de conquête des électeurs. Le Parti a pu renforcer son capital de marque par l’adhésion d’une personnalité disposant d’un fort capital de notoriété, l’objectif ultime consistait alors à associer les perceptions favorables de Lekjaa au PAM, en transférant vers son image les attributs et les associations positives liés à sa personnalité et sa performance dans les domaines et les missions qui lui ont été confiées: sa notoriété (forte reconnaissance publique), ses compétences (Gestion budgétaire, expertise financière et sportive), son leadership (Capacité à diriger et à porter des projets de grande envergure), sa performance (Résultats obtenus dans le domaine sportif/ le développement du football marocain), ainsi que sa visibilité et son rayonnement international (Forte exposition médiatique et présence dans les instances sportives internationales). Ce phénomène est appelé en marketing « le transfert d’image ou le brand image transfer », qui désigne le mécanisme par lequel les associations positives liées à une personne, une marque ou une organisation sont transférées vers une autre marque lorsqu’elles sont mises en relation. En outre, le transfert d'image ne consiste pas simplement à importer les associations d’une personnalité et les attribuer au parti. Le processus est beaucoup plus complexe. Il faut qu'il y ait une compatibilité entre l'image de la personnalité et le positionnement souhaité du parti. On parle alors de congruence d'image ou de fit entre la personnalité et la marque. La congruence d’image repose d’abord sur la compatibilité des valeurs associées à la personnalité avec celle que le parti souhaite promouvoir. Donc, pour réussir le transfert, les électeurs ne devraient percevoir aucune contradiction entre l’image de la personnalité et le positionnement du parti, sinon l’adhésion pourrait susciter des interrogations et fragiliser la crédibilité du rapprochement. La congruence d’image devrait également reposer sur la compatibilité des compétences qui renvoie à la correspondance entre les compétences reconnues à la personnalité et le positionnement du parti. En outre, la congruence d’image doit surtout reposer sur la congruence de la cible électorale, c'est-à-dire la compatibilité entre les publics auxquels la personnalité s’adresse et les segments de citoyens que le parti cherche à mobiliser : une personnalité bénéficiant d’une forte notoriété auprès des jeunes et des citoyens sensibles aux résultats concrets plutôt qu’aux discours idéologiques, peut contribuer à rendre le parti plus visible auprès de cette cible électorale. Le PAM a surtout misé sur les deux dernières dimensions de la congruence d’image entre la personnalité 'Lekjaa' et la marque 'le parti', à savoir la congruence des compétences et de la cible électorale. Donc en plus des campagnes axées autour de la personnalité de Lekjaa, la valorisation des compétences et des qualifications du parti, a constitué un axe majeur de son marketing politique. Rappelons que le PAM, depuis sa création, a toujours cherché à se présenter comme un parti ouvert aux compétences et aux profils technocratiques notamment durant l’ère de Mustapha El Bakkoury. En outre, le PAM, a cherché dans sa campagne pré-électorale et électorale à associer son identité à des valeurs telles que l’expertise, l’efficacité, la capacité de gestion et l’aptitude à concevoir et mettre en œuvre des politiques publiques. Cette orientation a contribué à construire une représentation du parti comme une formation disposant des ressources humaines capables d’assumer les responsabilités gouvernementales et de répondre aux enjeux économiques, sociaux et institutionnels. Dans cette perspective, la valorisation des compétences ne se limitait pas à la présentation du programme politique, elle visait également la construction d’une promesse de performance qui devient alors un élément majeur du positionnement du parti, permettant de différencier son image à travers la mise en avant de profils disposant d’une expertise professionnelle, technique ou institutionnelle. Le parti cherchait donc à construire une marque politique associée à la bonne gouvernance, à la compétence, à la modernisation et à la responsabilité, plutôt qu’à se limiter à une communication politique fondée sur des promesses électorales. Notons que le PAM avait placé « la bonne gouvernance » parmi ses axes les plus importants depuis la campagne électorale de 2021, en proposant la modernisation des politiques publiques, la reddition des comptes, la restructuration des finances publiques, l’optimisation des dépenses et la digitalisation de l’administration publique. Cette stratégie a permis au parti de renforcer sa perception par la cible électorale comme un parti orienté vers la gouvernance et la recherche de profils capables d’assumer pleinement des responsabilités de gestion publique, et de se différencier de ses concurrents en consolidant son image, à travers un positionnement explicitement centré sur la probité publique et la bonne gouvernance. L’arrivée de Lakjaâ comme une source de crédibilité managériale a renforcé ce positionnement en envoyant un message fort qui vise à réancrer l’identité du parti comme étant un parti qui attire les élites administratives et les gestionnaires performants. Il faut également souligner l’importance de l’effet surprise en marketing politique et électoral, qui consiste à intégrer des élements ou des personnages inattendus dans les campganes pour déclencher des réactions et des émotions fortes, mémorables et surtout rentables le jour du scrutin. L’adhésion est intervenue dans une période où les partis politiques commençaient à repenser leurs positionnements et leurs alliances, elle a donc fortement bouleversé leurs plans et perturbé leurs calculs. Dans ce contexte, leurs réactions ont été assez contrastées, mais la réaction la plus critique fut celle de Abdelilah Benkirane (PJD) qui a interprété l’arrivée de Lekjaa comme pouvant viser à contrer le PJD, dans le contexte de la reprise d’activité de son parti. La position du RNI a également était critique : Akhannouch a considéré ladite adhésion comme un « mercato » électoral, et Rachid Talbi Alami a critiqué la logique du « SHOW » et du « BUZZ » liée à cette polarisation, Aujjar, de son côté, a déclaré que « la politique et la démocratie sont différentes du football » . Tandis que les positions du parti de l’Istiklal, de l’USFP et du PPS ont été plus ouvertes : Ryad Mezzour membre de la direction de l’Istiqlal avait qualifié l’adhésion d’indicateur positif traduisant l’intégration d’une compétence technocratique à la vie politique, ceci a donc déclenché les premiers signaux de l’éventuelle recomposition politique qui pourrait constituer la nouvelle configuration gouvernementale post-éléctoral autour du PAM, de l’Istiqlal, de l’USFP et du PPS, Néanmoins, il faut signaler que toute stratégie de personnalisation ou de transfert de marque comporte aussi des risques liés notamment à la dépendance excessive à une figure individuelle, aux critiques sur le mélange entre technocratie et politique ; ou même aux attentes très élevées des citoyens. Donc durant ces élections, le PAM a été appelé plus que jamais à renforcer la coordination et la cohérence de sa communication politique autour de la loi de la sécurité maximale, selon laquelle les conseillers en marketing politique s’interdisent en théorie de prévenir ou d’anticiper sur un événement à venir si sa probabilité de réalisation n’est pas absolue, et de ne jamais parier sur un indice économique si les renseignements préalables à sa publication ne permettent pas dans quel sens il évoluerait. Rappelons dans ce sens que John McCAin a perdu en 2008 une grande partie de sa crédibilité lors de sa campagne électorale dans sa course à la présidentielle face à Barack Obama suite à sa déclaration affirmative que « les fondements de l’économie américaine étaient encore solides » alors que la banque Lehman Brothers était en train de s’effondre et de faire faillite déclenchant le jour même le krach de la bourse connu sous le nom « black Monday » ou le Lundi noir. Fouzi lakjaa s’est montré particulièrement prudent dans ses interventions lors de son soutien aux candidats du PAM durant leurs campagnes électorales. Toutefois, deux de ses prises de parole ont suscité un débat sur les réseaux sociaux, la première concerne son affirmation relative à l’organisation par le Maroc de la finale de la coupe du monde 2030 organisée conjointement avec l’Espagne et le Portugal. Cette déclaration est intervenue alors que, selon les informations disponibles à ce moment là, la FIFA n’avait pas encore officiellement arrêté le lieu de la finale. Cette prise de position a été perçue comme une anticipation d’une décision qui relève de l’instance internationale. La seconde intervention ayant suscité la polémique concerne le défi lancé au RNI lors de son meeting du 5 septembre à DAKHLA, portant notamment sur la proposition de revalorisation du SMIG. L’objectif de Lekjaa était de mettre le RNI face à ses propres engagements et de l’inciter à concrétiser sa proposition avant les élections. Toutefois, la formulation de cette intervention a pu être interprétée par une partie de l’opinion publique comme un engagement du PAM lui-même. Ces deux situations illustrent un risque de communication politique, lorsque la frontière entre la prise de position personnelle d’une personnalité n’est pas suffisamment claire, elle peut créer une confusion quant aux engagements réels de la marque politique-le parti politique-, car plus la personnalité est fortement médiatisée, plus ses déclarations peuvent être spontanément associées au parti, même lorsqu’elles ne constituent pas formellement un engagement programmatique. Le parti s’est rattrapé ensuite, en clarifiant, deux jours avant les élections, que l’augmentation du SMIG à 5.000 Dhs ne constitue pas un engagement de son programme électoral, et que ladite déclaration traduisait une façon de mettre le RNI au défi de concrétiser sa propre proposition avant les élections. Nous considérons donc l’adhésion de Fouzi Lekjaa au PAM comme un facteur qui a fortement contribué au renforcement de l’attractivité électorale du parti. Sa forte notoriété, et son image associée au développement du football national ont permis au PAM de bénéficier d’un capital d’image supplémentaire, mais il serait méthodologiquement excessif d’attribuer la progression électorale du parti qui s’inscrit dans un ensemble de facteurs politiques, électoraux et organisationnels à la seule adhésion de Lekjaa qui s'impose surtout comme un acteur stratégique incontournable pour l'ingénierie du futur exécutif, fort de son profil de technocrate chevronné et de gestionnaire des grands chantiers. Le succès électoral du PAM doit ouvrir une nouvelle phase dans laquelle le parti devrait transformer son capital de marque et la notoriété de ses personnalités, renforcée par l’adhésion de Fouzi Lekjaa, en capital de confiance institutionnelle. Cette transition nécessite le passage d’une logique de promotion politique à une logique de communication gouvernementale fondée sur la transparence, l’évaluation des résultats et la proximité avec les citoyens. *Docteure en marketing politique The post Lekjaa a-t-il réussi à conduire le PAM à bon port ? appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: Dakar Dem Dikk : Modou Bara Gaye prend la direction générale, cap sur la multimodalité
items.description: Dakar Dem Dikk a un nouveau patron. Dans un communiqué publié ce 09 octobre 2026, la société annonce que M. Modou Bara Gaye « a pris officiellement fonction en tant que Directeur Général de Dem Dikk SA ». Sa nomination intervient sur proposition du ministre des Transports Terrestres et Aériens, M. Lahat Ndiaye, et par décret du Président de la République, Bassirou Diomaye Faye. La communication précise que cette mission « est ancrée dans la Vision Sénégal 2050 », et « plus particulièrement son Objectif 3.5 », qui vise « un système de transport multimodal intégré ». Trois jalons sont fixés : Multimodalité : « Intégration totale DDD / TER / BRT avec le CETUD » ; Désenclavement : « Réponse à la demande des zones récemment urbanisées » ; Digitalisation : « Déploiement d'un paiement mobile fiable et d'une information voyageuse en temps réel », avec « un point d'attention particulier sur la cybersécurité ». Les JOJ en ligne de mire La nouvelle direction a déjà un rendez-vous à l'horizon : les Jeux Olympiques de la Jeunesse Dakar 2026. « Le défi est simple », écrit la société : « L'Afrique accueille, Dakar célèbre et Dem Dikk transporte. » Le communiqué adresse aussi un message interne. « À tous les agents et à tous les partenaires sociaux, un dialogue permanent est proposé en toute transparence et dans le strict respect de la mission de service public. »

items.title: Meurtre à Nabeul | L’ami de la victime interpellé à la Cité Ettahrir
items.description: L'enquête pour meurtre ouverte à Nabeul a permis l'arrestation à la Cité Ettahrir (à Tunis) du suspect, qui n'est autre que l'ami de la victime. Les agents de la brigade de la police judiciaire du Bardo sont parvenus à mettre la main sur le suspect principal recherché pour meurtre, indique Mosaïque FM, citant une source proche du dossier. Les investigations ont révélé que les deux hommes, qui se connaissaient, avaient planifié une traversée irrégulière vers les côtes européennes depuis Nabeul, en compagnie de cinq autres personnes. Mais une dispute liée aux préparatifs de la traversée irrégulière a éclaté entre les deux amis, virant au drame et coûtant la vie à la victime. Le suspect a quant à lui pris la fuite avant d'être localisé dans la maison où il se cachait à la Cité Ettahrir, puis arrêté par la police judiciaire du Bardo. items.title: Public Execution Won’t Have the Effect Trump Intends
items.description: Before the mid-19th century, executions in America were presumptively public. Most prisoners were hanged on a gallows, following an hours-long affair that began with the condemned person’s exit from jail accompanied by ministers, the sheriff and his deputies, and sometimes a military escort. Spectators joined the humiliating procession, gathering by the thousands to watch the noose lowered over the prisoner’s neck. The sheriff would mount the scaffold to read aloud the death warrant, sometimes adding commentary, and at least one minister (often several) would issue sermons. The condemned was offered the chance to give a speech, with spectators standing so close that they could ask the prisoner questions and join him in prayer, or bid him goodbye, if he was a family member or friend. All of that seemed safely confined to a past that the Trump administration now hopes to revive. President Trump, a consummate showman, has authorized the country’s first public execution in 90 years. The condemned prisoner is Nidal Hasan, a military psychiatrist who murdered 13 people and injured many more during a 2009 mass shooting at Fort Hood, in Texas. Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth has said that the killing, scheduled for December 3, will be conducted by the military and publicly livestreamed. During his trial, Hasan alarmed his standby attorneys when he chose to defend himself, and mounted an argument that the lawyers considered tantamount to seeking his own death. He could still conceivably file civilian appeals, which could delay his execution substantially. If it goes forward, the administration surely hopes to make an example of Hasan to all who might be tempted by his worldview. But this strategy could just as likely result in unintended consequences, and pushback by the public. [ Elizabeth Bruenig: The way of the gun ] Public executions ceased not because those who clamored to witness them found the displays uniformly outrageous, but because politicians in the 19th century associated them with proletarian barbarity. Though these executions were theoretically meant to deter crime and exhort onlookers to practice proper Christian values, they were mostly entertainment, and did not always provoke the desired reactions. Some onlookers cheered and celebrated the killings; others sympathized with the condemned. Public executions of Black prisoners in the South, for instance, became opportunities for community, song, and displays of Black religious authority. Ministers preached sermons of salvation and sometimes protested that the prisoners were innocent. In that sense, the public nature of executions backfired, and critics took note. Because the attendant crowds were so volatile, vulgar, and unruly, by 1860 all northern states had begun carrying out the killings in jail yards, which were much smaller areas, subject to tight government control. Decades later, the South followed suit. The large crowds soon vanished. Military executions, traditionally carried out by firing squad, were long conducted in small, controlled settings, often witnessed only by military personnel and chaplains. The last military execution in the United States was carried out in 1961. Trump and Hegseth aim to have it both ways: a small, secure setting and massive crowds. This time, viewers will be watching a livestream on their screens, close enough to see the event but too far to smell the gunpowder. Both Hegseth and Trump seem intent on flexing America’s political power and military might as a message not just to foreign enemies but to the American people, as if to say: This could be you. This method of ruling by fear is central to authoritarian governance, and Trump and Hegseth seem drawn to executions partly for that reason. But if Trump and Hegseth are hoping for a deterrent effect, they’re unlikely to get it. The idea that executions could deter other killers with political motives seems sorely mistaken; those who carry out such murders already know that they could face grave consequences, and have deemed that outcome acceptable. Nor do executions deter murderers without political motives, because deterrence is generated not by the severity of the punishment, but by the certainty of getting caught. And there is little certainty in American homicide investigations: In 2023, the nationwide case-clearance rate for murder was only 58 percent, meaning that murderers have decent odds of evading justice. Even if they are caught, they have good odds of avoiding the death penalty—only 23 new death sentences were handed down in 2025. Trump’s Department of Justice hopes to boost those numbers, but even if they tripled, they would add up to 69 death sentences spread across some 14,000 murders. [ Read: The problem with Trump’s crime claims ] Adding a livestreamed element is perhaps an attempt to intensify the intended deterrent effect, but it might have opposite consequences. Plenty of Americans would surely enjoy the spectacle of a public execution, just as people have historically. One can envision groups of people crowded around their phones, sharing chips and drinks, admiring the military pageantry. But it’s easy to imagine a different effect, too: Other crowds of people, other phones, entirely different impressions—that the death penalty is a disgusting violation of human rights that puts America in league with nations such as Saudi Arabia, Iran, and China. Or that Nidal Hasan is a martyr, and the United States is a savage country not worth defending—which is the narrative presented by Hasan himself. Before the shooting, he told family that he’d turned against the country he served upon hearing horrific stories of war from his psychiatric patients, and grew troubled by the fact that America was killing Muslims abroad. Carrying out his public execution would only credit the notion that this country is barbarous.

items.title: Truck crushes Ondo VIO official to death, driver arrested
items.description: By Dayo Johnson, Akure A 35-year-old Vehicle Inspection Officer (VIO), Adediji Sesan, has been crushed to death by a vehicle along Hospital Road, opposite Mega Primary School, Akure, the Ondo State capital. The driver of the vehicle, identified as 37-year-old Ayoade Idowu, has been arrested and detained by the police in connection with the incident. It was gathered that Sesan was on routine patrol with his team when he attempted to stop a white Mitsubishi van with registration number AGL 992 XX for document inspection. According to an eyewitness, the driver initially stopped but allegedly drove off when asked to produce the relevant documents, hitting the VIO official in the process. The victim reportedly sustained severe head injuries and was rushed to the Federal University of Technology Akure (FUTA) Teaching Hospital, where a doctor on duty confirmed him dead. His remains have been deposited at the hospital mortuary for preservation and autopsy. Confirming the incident, the spokesperson for the Ondo State Police Command, DSP Jimoh Abayomi, said the driver had been arrested and detained while preliminary investigations were ongoing. Abayomi said police operatives had visited the scene and commenced investigations into the circumstances surrounding the incident. He added that the case file was expected to be transferred to the Motor Traffic Division for further investigation. The police spokesman expressed condolences to the family, colleagues and associates of the deceased, assuring them that a thorough investigation would be conducted and appropriate legal action taken in accordance with the law. He urged motorists to exercise patience, obey lawful traffic instructions and cooperate with authorised traffic enforcement officers. “No road user should endanger the life of another in an attempt to evade routine checks or traffic regulations,” he warned. Abayomi reiterated the command’s commitment to ensuring road safety, protecting lives and property, and maintaining law and order across the state. The post Truck crushes Ondo VIO official to death, driver arrested appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: INEC begins voters’ register display, PVC distribution in Borno
items.description: By Ndahi Marama, Maiduguri The Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) in Borno State has commenced the display of the voters’ register and distribution of Permanent Voter Cards (PVCs) across the state’s 27 local government areas. The Head of Voter Education and Publicity in the state, Ibrahim Shuaibu, said the display of the register and distribution of PVCs would be conducted in phases, with the commission providing timelines for claims and objections. Shuaibu said the exercise would be extended to the ward level to ensure wider participation and enable registered voters to verify their details. “The display and distribution of PVCs will take place simultaneously across the 27 local government areas of the state,” he said. He expressed satisfaction with the turnout of residents who had visited designated centres to check their names on the register and collect their PVCs. According to him, the ongoing distribution covers voters who participated in the registration exercises conducted in August and December last year. He added that INEC was awaiting the delivery of additional PVCs from the commission’s national headquarters. items.title: Le groupe chinois Hangyu Technology délaisse la Slovaquie au profit du Maroc
items.description: Le groupe chinois Hangyu Technology a décidé de s'implémenter au Maroc, à Tanger Tech, plutôt qu’en Slovaquie, en construisant une usine pour un investissement de 105 millions d'euros. L’objectif est de construire une usine spécialisée dans la fabrication de pièces métalliques de haute précision destinées notamment à l’aéronautique et à l’énergie. Elle doit notamment produire des pièces métalliques forgées, notamment des anneaux et des composants capables de résister à des températures élevées et à des contraintes mécaniques importantes. Ces pièces peuvent servir aux moteurs d’avion, aux turbines à gaz et à différents équipements industriels et devraient servir les ambitions du groupe de se développer au plus près de ses clients internationaux, notamment en Europe, aux Etats-Unis et au Moyen-Orient. Si le projet initial devait se faire en Slovaquie, il a été transféré au Maroc pour cause d'un contrôle administratif supplémentaire en cours de procédure, rallongeant les délais et impactant le plan de développement. Le fabricant chinois Hangyu Technology devrait donc s'installer dans la Cité Mohammed VI Tanger Tech, au lieu de construire son usine en Slovaquie. Si le projet avait déjà démarré avec la création d'une filiale locale, la signature d'une promesse d'acquisition d'un terrain industriel, la procédure administrative supplémentaire aurait fait éclater le deal. L'entreprise soutient qu'aucune procédure administrative supplémentaire et similaire ne serait ajoutée au Maroc, et que les conditions d’accompagnement du projet étaient déjà réunies. Réuni le 8 octobre 2026, le conseil d’administration du groupe a retenu la Cité Mohammed VI Tanger Tech pour accueillir cette base de production. Une société baptisée à titre provisoire Atlas Advanced Materials LLC pilotera l'implémentation et sera détenue par une filiale de Sichuan Delan Hangyu, détenue par le groupe Hangyu Technology. Le groupe devrait injecter environ 40 millions d'euros, soit 300 millions de yuans à Sichuan Delan Hangyu, soit l’équivalent de 34,8% du budget maximal annoncé pour l’usine marocaine. Cette enveloppe devrait être versée de façon progressive. Par ailleurs, le projet initialement prévu en Slovaquie devait créer 335 emplois, dont 192 postes directement liés à la production et 143 fonctions administratives, techniques, commerciales, logistiques ou de soutien, cependant ce chiffre n'est pas encore confirmé à ce stade pour le projet de Tanger. Par ailleurs, le terrain prévu en Slovaquie, près de Košice, devait porter sur une superficie de 150.204 mètres carrés, accompagnés de 42.000 mètres carrés de bâtiments industriels dans le cadre du dossier environnemental, mais ses contours au niveau du Maroc n'ont pas encore été annoncés alors que le calendrier du début des travaux sur le premier projet devait débuter en décembre pour un début d'exploitation en décembre 2028. The post Le groupe chinois Hangyu Technology délaisse la Slovaquie au profit du Maroc appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: Joy in Nayilifong as Farouk Aliu Mahama donates 100kVA transformer to improve power supply
items.description: Residents of Nayilifong, a community in the Yendi Constituency, have been thrown into wild jubilation following the donation of a 100kVA electricity transformer by former Member of Parliament for Yendi, Alhaji Farouk Aliu Mahama. The transformer, which arrived in the community on Wednesday, October 6, was met with rousing ecstasy as community members poured out in large numbers to witness the offloading. For months, Nayilifong has struggled with erratic power supply, affecting businesses, students, and households. Both the elderly and the youth could not hide their joy as the much-needed facility was unveiled, with many showering praises on the former MP for his continued generosity even after leaving office. “We cannot thank our son, Farouk Aliu Mahama, enough for his continuous support to us even after he lost the seat. May God bless him,” an elated woman said, echoing the sentiments of many residents. Legacy of service beyond parliament As MP for Yendi, Mr Aliu Mahama was credited with massive development projects in the areas of infrastructure, education, and youth empowerment. He, however, surprisingly lost his seat in the 2024 general elections. Since leaving Parliament, he has sustained his philanthropic activities across the constituency, refusing to abandon the people he once represented. Just a few weeks ago, he was widely applauded in Yendi for his generous financial support to a young medical student from the constituency to enable him to complete his studies. Residents say the latest intervention will not only stabilise electricity supply but also boost small-scale businesses that depend heavily on power.

items.title: Atiku’s attacks on Tinubu, signs of political depression — Keyamo
items.description: By Omeiza Ajayi ABUJA: Minister of Aviation and Aerospace Development, Festus Keyamo, SAN, on Friday night launched a blistering critique against former Vice President Atiku Abubakar, describing the opposition leader’s recent verbal broadsides against President Bola Tinubu as symptoms of “agitated depression” fueled by political defeat. In a statement, Keyamo argued that Atiku’s ongoing hostility toward the President stems from a deep-seated inability to accept the outcome of the 2023 presidential election. Keyamo claimed that the African Democratic Congress ADC presidential candidate feels outmaneuvered by President Tinubu, who secured the presidency on his first attempt after the two politicians pursued parallel, decades-long political trajectories. “It is now very obvious that Atiku Abubakar is a pained and very bitter fellow. The pain and bitterness stems from the fact that he feels President Bola Ahmed Tinubu finally outsmarted him politically to get the most coveted position of President and he can’t mentally deal with this fact”, he said. Tracing their political ties back to when Tinubu served as Governor of Lagos State and Atiku served as Vice President, Keyamo observed that Atiku was once viewed as higher in the political pecking order. However, he noted that through “fate, luck, divine intervention, and political dexterity,” Tinubu clinched the nation’s top office—a goal Atiku has pursued since 1993. Keyamo further called on those close to the former Vice President to offer him support rather than encouraging his public outbursts, adding that Atiku’s posture risks alienating his remaining supporters as he moves toward “political oblivion.” Invoking Ecclesiastes 9:11 to emphasize that political power is governed by divine timing, Keyamo declared that Atiku “urgently needs mental health support at this critical time.” The post Atiku’s attacks on Tinubu, signs of political depression — Keyamo appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: The Real Harm of a Public Execution
items.description: Yesterday, in an interview aboard the USS Abraham Lincoln, Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth said the United States would soon carry out its first public execution since the 1930s. “We’ll make sure that people are able to watch it,” he said. Pentagon officials later confirmed that the execution will be livestreamed. The condemned man is former Major Nidal Hasan, who shouted “God is great” in Arabic before murdering 13 people at Fort Hood in 2009. Hegseth’s rationale for following this ancient practice is the same one offered by the ancients themselves: publicizing the agony of death and its unhygienic aftermath will remind onlookers that, in Hegseth’s words, there are “serious consequences” for treason. “No-brainer,” Hegseth said. This pitiful creep—Hasan, I mean—deserves what he is probably going to get in December. The rest of us, however, will be ill-served by the spectacle of his execution. Many past criminals have had their head publicly cut off, or body nailed to a cross and left to rot there, as exemplary punishment. Such executions were once considered entertainment. Now the idea of recreationally watching a man be killed is so strange that few people understand what the experience will be like. Watching people die by violence, even if those people have it coming, damages the spectator irreversibly. I don’t mean physical or emotional damage, though many who see unnatural deaths up close do vomit and suffer from uneasy dreams afterward. Rather, I mean something more like the loss of their humanity and dignity, through partaking in the process of treating a person—in many ways so similar to themselves—like a machine to be turned off or ripped apart, a malfunctioning printer or an old car. To see this process is to be diminished, and the decision to make the execution visible to all is an invitation to self-harm, sent out to everyone with an internet connection. It is hard to appreciate how awful this viewing experience will be, until you have it. And then of course it will be too late. I have seen videotaped executions and have been diminished by every single one. In August 2014, Hasan wrote a letter from prison to Abu Bakr al-Baghdadi, then the leader of the Islamic State, and asked to be granted citizenship as a “soldier of Allah.” No response was recorded. Ironically, it seems likely that Hasan would sympathize with Hegseth’s penchant for public execution, because the Islamic State interpreted the Quran to require that execution be carried out in public. Fornicators, according to Quran 24:2, should be flogged, and their punishment should be “witnessed” by a “group of believers.” By extension, the Islamic State determined, such a group should witness the punishment of all scripturally ordained crimes. Certain crimes, such as brigandage, are to be punished with crucifixion, an inherently public method of killing that the Islamic State carried out on video. Regrettably, I have seen footage of such a death. [ From the July 2025 issue: Inside America’s death chambers ] In the years before Hasan’s 2013 court-martial, he stopped shaving, in Islamic defiance of Army regulations that prohibit soldiers from growing beards. Mike Simpson, an Army officer and emergency-room doctor near the facility where Hasan was incarcerated, told me a few years later that he put the word out to colleagues that if Hasan ever had a medical emergency (not unlikely, given that he suffered paralysis and other conditions after being gunned down in the course of his terror attack), Simpson would like to be called to shave Hasan personally. The shaving would arise out of medical necessity—the patient might need a mask, with a reliable seal around the face—but Simpson, for his own pleasure, wanted to shear the bastard himself. But the pleasure that might come from shaving Hasan would be quite different from what one might experience by shooting him in the heart. The Army won’t struggle to find a dozen willing soldiers to act as an execution party for Hasan. Hasan has said he wants death. Hegseth said he “doesn’t care” what Hasan’s final wishes might be. But I suspect that the volunteers’ enjoyment of their duty will be dampened if they notice signs of ecstasy from Hasan, as he is tied to a post 15 paces away from them and prays his way to the end. Hamlet could not bring himself to kill Claudius in prayer, because killing him in the midst of a holy act—“to take him in the purging of his soul, when he is fit and season’d for his passage”—would be too merciful. In this world, denying Hasan the pleasure of death on his own terms, and letting him instead spend a few more earthly decades in tedious incarceration, would seem a much more onerous punishment. Therefore I would propose an alternative to public execution: public incarceration. Hasan should be placed in a small space, with a Pentagon-funded livestream of his remaining years. If the purpose of the spectacle of his death is to demonstrate to others the “serious consequences” of murdering 13 people, I doubt any execution would be more frightening than the slow, public aging of this repulsive murderer, as biology and time carry out his sentence. I would tune in to the livestream myself now and then, until I grew bored and found better things to do, and better ways to spend my own remaining time. This would take Hasan’s life and make from it a small gift to the rest of us, rather than taking something irrecoverable from us as we give martyrdom to him.

items.title: Ouverture à Nouakchott d’une antenne de l’école marocaine des sciences de l’ingénierie
items.description: L'École marocaine des sciences de l'ingénierie a inauguré jeudi une antenne en Mauritanie, une initiative qui renforce la présence des établissements d'enseignement supérieur marocains dans le pays et propose de nouveaux programmes dans les domaines du génie civil, de la construction et de la gestion de projets. Le ministre de l’Enseignement supérieur et de la Recherche scientifique, Yacoub Ould Meïne, a présidé l’inauguration de cette antenne à Nouakchott, qui propose des spécialisations comprenant le génie civil, les travaux publics, la géotechnique et l’hydraulique urbaine, ainsi que les systèmes d’information de gestion de la construction. Ould Meïne a déclaré que l’ouverture de cette antenne reflétait la coopération entre la Mauritanie et le Maroc dans le domaine de l’enseignement supérieur, ajoutant que le développement de la formation et la diversification des spécialités figuraient parmi les objectifs des réformes en cours dans ce secteur. Le directeur général du groupe de l’École marocaine des sciences l'ingénierie, Mohamed El Rahabi, a indiqué que la succursale travaillerait en coordination avec des établissements d’enseignement mauritaniens, notamment l’École supérieure polytechnique et l’Institut supérieur de la numérisation, dans le but d’élargir l’offre de formation en ingénierie et de renforcer les échanges d’étudiants, d’enseignants et d’expertise. De son côté, le directeur général de la succursale en Mauritanie, Ahmed Salem Ould Abdel Raouf, a déclaré que l’établissement avait pour objectif de former des ingénieurs mauritaniens dans des domaines tels que la numérisation, l’intelligence artificielle, le génie civil et la construction. L’ambassadeur du Maroc en Mauritanie, Hamid Chabar, a quant à lui déclaré que l’ouverture de cette antenne reflétait la poursuite de la coopération entre les deux pays dans les domaines de l’éducation et de la formation, soulignant la volonté du Maroc de poursuivre cette coopération.

items.title: Linguère : Attaque à main armée à Gassane
items.description: Dans la nuit du jeudi 8 au vendredi 9 octobre 2026, aux environs de minuit, un couple de la localité de Gassane, dans le département de Linguère, a été violemment agressé par des voleurs de bétail. Armés de machettes, les assaillants ont tenté de s’emparer d'un troupeau de moutons. L'homme et son épouse, enceinte de neuf mois, ont été blessés. Les victimes ont été évacuées à Touba pour recevoir des soins. Selon des témoins, deux individus armés de machettes ont attaqué le couple qui tentait de protéger son troupeau. La femme, enceinte, a reçu un coup sur la tête et sur le bras, s'effondrant dans une mare de sang. Son époux, lui, a été atteint aux mains. Face à la gravité des blessures, les deux victimes ont été acheminées vers Touba pour une prise en charge médicale. L'état de la femme enceinte suscite une inquiétude dans la communauté. Les habitants de Gassane sont sous le choc. En effet, cette attaque ravive la peur des voleurs de bétail, un fléau récurrent dans le Ferlo, où les éleveurs vivent dans une insécurité croissante. Abdoulaye SADIO (Correspondant)

items.title: L’ambassadeur allemand en Mauritanie : « la coopération bilatérale entre les 2 pays une dynamique remarquable l’année dernière »
items.description: L'ambassadeur d'Allemagne en Mauritanie, Florian Reindel, a déclaré jeudi que les relations entre les deux pays avaient connu une dynamique remarquable au cours de l'année écoulée, qui s'est traduite par des échanges de visites de haut niveau, notamment celle du ministre allemand des Affaires étrangères en Mauritanie fin juillet dernier. Reindel a ajouté, lors d’une cérémonie organisée par l’ambassade d’Allemagne à Nouakchott à l’occasion de la Journée de l’unité allemande, que les relations entre les deux pays entraient dans leur soixante-sixième année, soulignant que la coopération bilatérale avait abouti à la mise en œuvre d’un certain nombre de projets de développement. L’ambassadeur a précisé que l’un des projets les plus marquants était l’inauguration du nouveau quai de la garde côtière mauritanienne à Nouadhibou, réalisé avec le soutien de la Banque allemande de coopération, soulignant l’engagement de l’Allemagne à fournir une enveloppe financière de 54 millions d’euros, dont une grande partie est consacrée à la formation professionnelle. Il a indiqué que son pays soutenait les efforts mauritaniens dans les domaines du climat et de l’immigration, ainsi que le renforcement du partenariat économique et d’investissement entre les deux pays. La cérémonie s’est déroulée en présence du ministre des Affaires étrangères, de la Coopération africaine et des Mauritaniens de l’extérieur, Mohamed Salem Ould Marzoug, ainsi que de plusieurs diplomates et responsables mauritaniens.
